word-noun.t: Every sentence needs a {noun} or a pronoun.
Can you find the {noun} in this sentence?

word-adjective.t: Use an {adjective} to describe the house.
The {adjective} usually comes before the noun in English.

word-adverb.t: An {adverb} can tell us how something happens.

word-pronoun.t: A {pronoun} helps us avoid repeating a name.

word-preposition.t: I always forget which {preposition} to use.
Choose the correct {preposition} for each sentence.

word-conjunction.t: Use a {conjunction} to join these two sentences.

word-article-grammar.t: Use the {article} 'an' before a vowel sound.
Many learners forget the {article} in English.

word-syllable.t: The stress is on the first {syllable}.

word-vowel.t: Every English word has at least one {vowel} sound.
Say the {vowel} in this word slowly.

word-consonant.t: This word has three {consonants} in a row.
Write the missing {consonant} in each word.

word-spelling.t: Check the {spelling} of this word in the dictionary.

word-pronunciation.t: The dictionary shows the {pronunciation} of each word.

word-tone-grammar.t: A different {tone} gives the word a different meaning.
It is hard to hear the {tone} at first.

word-synonym.t: Can you think of a {synonym} for 'happy'?

word-antonym.t: Can you think of an {antonym} for 'early'?

word-plural.t: Most English words add -s in the {plural}.
Write the {plural} form of each word.

word-grammatical-gender.t: German has three kinds of {grammatical gender}.
Learn the {grammatical gender} together with each new noun.

word-masculine.t: In French, the word for 'book' is {masculine}.
Many German words for jobs have a {masculine} form.

word-feminine.t: In Spanish, the word for 'house' is {feminine}.
Add an ending to make the word {feminine}.

word-neuter.t: In German, the word for 'girl' is {neuter}.
Some languages have a {neuter} form as well.
Is this noun masculine, feminine or {neuter}?

word-tense.t: The verb is in the wrong {tense}.

word-past-tense.t: Put these sentences in the {past tense}.
Add -ed to form the {past tense} of regular verbs.

word-present-tense.t: We use the {present tense} for daily habits.
Change the verb to the {present tense}.

word-future-tense.t: Use the {future tense} to talk about tomorrow.
Write three sentences in the {future tense}.

word-grammatical-case.t: The {grammatical case} of this noun is genitive.
English only uses {case} for some pronouns.

word-conjugation.t: The {conjugation} of this verb is irregular.
Study the {conjugation} table on page ten.

word-declension.t: Learning {declension} takes a lot of practice.
This table shows the full {declension} of the word.

word-infinitive.t: The dictionary lists verbs in the {infinitive}.
Change the verb to the {infinitive} form.

word-punctuation.t: Don't forget the {punctuation} at the end.
Add the missing {punctuation} to this sentence.

word-comma.t: Put a {comma} after the first word.
You need a {comma} between the two names.
I often forget the {comma} in long sentences.

word-full-stop.t: Put a {period} at the end of the sentence.
I forgot the {period} after the last word.

word-question-mark.t: Put a {question mark} at the end.
A {question mark} shows that someone is asking something.

word-capital-letter.t: Start every sentence with a {capital letter}.
Names always begin with a {capital letter}.
Write your last name in {capital letters}.

word-vocabulary.t: She has a very large English {vocabulary}.
I learn ten new {vocabulary} words every day.
Reading is a good way to build your {vocabulary}.

word-idiom.t: 'It's raining cats and dogs' is an {idiom}.

word-slang-word.t: Teenagers often use a lot of {slang}.
That word is {slang}, not formal English.
Don't use {slang} in a job interview.

word-dialect.t: People in the south speak a different {dialect}.
This word is only used in one {dialect}.
I find her {dialect} hard to understand.

word-native-speaker.t: My teacher is a {native speaker} of English.
A {native speaker} would say it differently.
I want to practice with a {native speaker}.

word-mother-tongue.t: Children learn their {mother tongue} at home.

word-foreign-language.t: We study a {foreign language} at school.

word-fluent.t: After two years, he became {fluent} in Spanish.
I want to be {fluent} in English.

word-translator.t: The {translator} helped us at the meeting.

word-exercise-task.t: This {exercise} is too easy for me.
The teacher gave us a grammar {exercise}.

word-textbook.t: I forgot my math {textbook} at home.

word-flashcard.t: I make a {flashcard} for every new word.
She studies with {flashcards} on the bus.
Turn over the {flashcard} to see the answer.

word-beginner.t: He is a {beginner} at the piano.

word-advanced.t: This book is too {advanced} for me.

word-intermediate.t: My English is at an {intermediate} level.

word-reading.t: Her {reading} in English is getting better.
We have a {reading} test on Friday.

word-writing.t: {Writing} in English is difficult for me.

word-listening.t: {Listening} is harder than reading for me.
Good {listening} is important in any language.

word-memorize.t: I {memorize} ten new words every day.
It's hard to {memorize} so many dates.

word-stress-accent.t: The {stress} is on the second syllable.
Where does the {stress} fall in this word?
Wrong {stress} can make a word hard to understand.

word-expression.t: This {expression} is very common in English.
